💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row.
  • This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be.
  • It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

In a recent development, spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur.

It has been revealed that did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

Recent findings suggest that “I am really aware of the situation,” Sage mentioned. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”.

It has been revealed that the decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

According to recent reports, the challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

Sources indicate that it was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be stated of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

Jean-Philippe Mateta receives his first red card for Crystal Palace! 🟥 https://t.co/U9UYb29mbk.

All of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

Sources indicate that “Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi mentioned. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We highlighted our maturity. We are improving.”.

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

Jan Paul van Hecke doubles Spurs' lead! 👊 https://t.co/1Odkkr8wBJ.

The new signings at Spurs endured a difficult first few weeks but there were more signs here that they are adjusting to De Zerbi’s system. Sandro Tonali was exceptional in midfield and teenage talent Luca Williams-Barnett also sparkled off the bench. “Tonali was unbelievable,” De Zerbi said. “We played with two players more: Tonali was double.”.

Spurs face Leeds United, Ipswich Town, Sunderland and Fulham in their next four league games. The momentum could, and perhaps should, continue to build. Their optimism here contrasted sharply with the angst of Palace, and with the troubled look that was etched on Sage’s face.

“Very pleased for the performance, very tough game. You don’t know 11 [against 11] would be different game but Crystal Palace are very tough because they defend with a low block, no space and we highlighted we are a mature team. Maybe we could score more goals with more nastiness, but I am very happy because we created many chances. We need more goals for sure. It’s not enough, but we are improving a lot.

Sources indicate that “I was very nervous before the game, during the game, after the red card, it’s always better playing with one player more. But today, against this team, they played with this behaviour, all behind the line of the ball, aggressive. Very tough game.”.

When asked if Spurs are looking up the table, he replied: “We don’t forget the ambitions. We have to look behind what was the situation two weeks ago. In the last two years, two times 17th in the table, many games without a win in front of our fans. We have to stay focused. They are improving, increasing the level of performance.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Palace defender said: “Definitely was frustrating. It was one of the first tackles of the game. And we felt like we were doing well and it is unfortunate. We go again.

In a recent development, “The main message was don’t concede again, stay tight as a defence and try to hit them on the counter. That is the best initiative when you’re down a man.

“Unfortunately, it didn’t happen today. We know what we can do as a team, as a back five, the whole unit. There were some positives in the games, but I can’t say much when you lose. We just have to go again.

Industry observers note that “Hopefully, the next game we win. The main message is to stay together as a team. We know what we are capable of. It is staying confident and bouncing back.”.

"We want to be back at the top again" Jan Paul van Hecke reacts after Spurs win three consecutive Premier League games ⚪ https://t.co/XXOeOKLhoC.

Tottenham have won three Premier League games in a row for the first time in 616 days 📆 https://t.co/krb7tkrPyM.

Job done for Spurs, who now have three successive Premier League wins thanks to this routine victory over 10-man Palace. Headers from defensive duo Gray and Van Hecke settled the contest. It was a tricky evening for the visitors and they were left with a mountain to climb following Mateta’s early red card. Tottenham are up to eighth, while Palace are in the relegation zone on goal difference.

FULL-TIME: Spurs make it three Premier League wins in a row! ✅ https://t.co/b44TNkBhqT.

Kulusevski cuts inside and whips a shot towards the far top corner, but Henderson is there to make a sensational save and parry it away. Every Tottenham fan wanted that to nestle in the net.

Williams-Barnett is denied a dream debut assist. Out wide on the left, the 18-year-old glides away from a couple of challenges to reach the byline and tee up Kudus, who fluffs the opportunity by directing his close-range effort wide.

There will be three minutes of added time to end this game.

Industry observers note that pedro Porro continues to venture forward and smacks a half-volley over from a tight angle. Spurs make the game’s next change as former Palace loanee Gallagher replaces Solanke, with Marmoush moving up into the striker position.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

Sources indicate that in his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (849 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.
  • Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice.
  • According to recent reports, "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related issues and the athletic performance of individual players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

"Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was launched.

According to recent reports, "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related issues and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.

"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent.".

The fan club states their issue is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club stated "gives us cause to reassess the situation.".

Recent findings suggest that this campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (SIGNIFICANT) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.

Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:.

"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

"My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold.".

Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.

Recent findings suggest that the fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends.".

Here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's strategy" and that homosexuality is a sin.

Sources indicate that borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone.".

Sources indicate that article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

The use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Significant-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit.".

And yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the new opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.

With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the controversy surrounding Jamal Musiala is far from falling on Bayern Munich. For several days, the Bavarian management’s comments on the future of the attacking midfielder and his imposing salary have sparked a wave of indignation in Germany. After Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, it is now Maik Franz who has stepped up to the plate. Guest of the show Doppelpass on Sport1the former defender did not mince his words to denounce the attitude of the Munich board, which he considers particularly inappropriate towards a player facing health problems. At the heart of this controversy, the statements of Rummenigge, who publicly questioned Musiala’s salary conditions in view of his physical difficulties and his level of performance.

Industry observers note that an outing which provoked numerous reactions, notably from Maik Franz: “what the Bayern leaders are doing, and I’m not talking about Kompany and Eberl, who are behaving in an exemplary manner, but about MM. Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge, is pathetic and even, in my eyes, constitutes harassment. We can discuss a player’s performance. But it is not appropriate to talk publicly about an illness and the salary associated with it, at this level. We must not forget that Jamal tried everything to come back. He indicated a lot of courage and transparency in discussing his diagnosis. For this to turn against him today is not acceptable. To be completely honest, we are no longer in “Mia san Mia”, but in “Mia san money”. Money takes precedence over people. And this must not happen.”.

The controversy even went beyond the borders of Bavarian management to affect the locker room. Michael Olise actually liked an Instagram post from Fabrizio Romano relaying the press release from FIFPRO, the international players’ union, which called on Bayern to respect Jamal Musiala. A particularly notable gesture from the French international, renowned for his discretion on social networks. This support takes on an additional dimension as Bayern wish to extend Olise’s contract, at the moment linked to the club until 2029. Maik Franz also underlined the risk that this affair could represent for decision-makers: “With Michael Olise, you may have the next best player in the world in your ranks. He too must extend and receive a significant salary. But you keep in mind that if you got sick or injured and didn’t perform, you would be publicly thrown out to waste. Frankly, I don’t think they did themselves any favors.”.

According to recent reports, FIFPRO also strongly criticized Bayern’s communication, saying contractual issues should be discussed privately with the player and his representatives. The union notably recalled that an injury or decline in form did not justify publicly calling into question salary conditions already agreed upon. While Musiala tries to regain his best level after a long period of absence, the Bavarian club finds itself under fire from critics. Between the declarations of its leaders, the exit of Maik Franz and the remarkable gesture of Olise, the file has become a real image glitch for Bayern Munich….

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, attention is turning to the much smaller company she worked for.

Sources indicate that alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing firm. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba.

It has been revealed that according to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the firm advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations. Megaspeed says it provides access for clients to Nvidia's advanced GB200 NVL72 ​computing system.

This type of firm is often referred to as a "neocloud". It buys Nvidia chips and computing power and then rents it out — in this case, at multiple sites across south-east Asia, to different companies. The US has set up strict export controls to prevent that Nvidia's high-performance chips end up in China, because it sees China as a competitor in the global AI race. It also does not want data centers made up of Nvidia chips to be owned by Chinese companies. It does, however, tolerate that data center compute with Nvidia chips be rented out to Chinese companies like Alibaba, and occasionally allows the export of Nvidia chips for specific purposes.

Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia's products in recent years and has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China.

In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that the "once-obscure" Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in all of south-east Asia and that the US government was investigating its ownership structure and whether or not it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

At the same time, Singapore police began an investigation into whether or not Megaspeed had "violated local laws" without specifying which ones. Those investigations are believed to be still ongoing.

On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement — which still appears as the first page for visitors to the company's website as of November 2026.

It has been revealed that "There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate organization," it said. "We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct.".

The US government investigation began in 2024. The Commerce Department initially began looking into Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over. According to the Fresh York Times, this switch came about after an Nvidia executive directly contacted the Commerce Department about the investigation.

Megaspeed was founded in 2015 and was originally called 7Road International. It changed its name to Megaspeed in March 2023. It is owned by the Singapore-registered Swiftdata, which was set up in October 2023.

Its rise in prominence coincided with a sharp increase in assets, which increased from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024.

In a recent development, alice H., the woman accused of being a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is widely seen as an influential figurehead at Megaspeed. She also served as the manufacturer's managing director of Megaspeed for eight months in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that the Financial Times reported on Monday that Alice H. leveraged her close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia to pitch AI chips deals to Chinese investors.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the newspaper remarked that in early 2025, Alice H. sought investment in China for a data center project in south-east Asia, and cited their easy access to Nvidia chips and close relationship with Alibaba.

It has been revealed that alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024, via subsidiaries. It has remained Megaspeed's largest client, according to reporting by the Financial Times.

According to recent reports, in December 2025, Nvidia noted its own inquiry into Megaspeed had found no evidence of chips being diverted and that the company was fully owned and operated outside of China, with no Chinese shareholders. The company told Bloomberg at the time that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities on multiple occasions and had seen nothing untoward.

Megaspeed is one of several companies accused of smuggling Nvidia's chips into China or finding ways to give Chinese companies access to them.

Nvidia's high-performance chips are seen as essential for companies looking for the most advanced form of supercomputing to use and develop various AI applications.

Back in 2022, the Biden Administration began severely restricting the sale of the US's most advanced chips to China, part of the two countries' growing rivalry to achieve AI dominance.

However, an illegal smuggling and underground network was soon set up, with many vendors operating to get the chips into China and selling them on to companies there.

In December 2025, US authorities shut down the operations of Hao Global, a US-based shell firm with links to China which plead guilty to smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

In June 2026, Taiwanese government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer as part of an investigation into the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China.

While export restrictions have been eased significantly under the Trump administration, there are still significant blocks and restrictions on the most advanced Nvidia chips.

In December 2025, the Trump administration approved several Chinese companies to buy or handle advanced Nvidia H200 chips, a move that sparked significant concern among the US security establishment.

However, that deal has not led to a significant flow of Nvidia chips moving legally to China, amid strict US licencing controls and official reluctance from Beijing to publicly promote Nvidia chips to the detriment of its own alternatives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's no secret that getting playing time is vital to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country . For most national team coaches, only a keeper who is playing regularly for his club merits consideration.

Recent findings suggest that unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception. While he did give Urbig – the backup keeper at Bayern – two starts in his first international break as national team boss, for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen remains the undisputed No. 1.

According to recent reports, but when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich. But this is set to change after Bayern's recent Bundesliga win over Mainz. The 40-year-old Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off just before halftime, complaining of severe pain in his right foot.

An examination revealed that Neuer has sustained a partial tendon tear in the foot.

"An injury never comes at the right time, but it's part of the game," Neuer wrote on Instagram.

"I've been through this before, and I'll get through this one too. From now on: full focus on recovery. Until then, I will support the boys on the pitch wherever I can.".

It has been revealed that A partial tendon tear usually results in a layoff of six to 12 weeks, depending on the severity of the injury. Given that Neuer's foot already has some pre-existing damage from previous injuries, his recovery could take even longer.

Although Urbig is now the de-facto first-choice keeper for Bayern, he will still have to bide his time in the national team as understudy to ter Stegen. However, there is a general consensus that someday, Urbig will also become Germany's No. 1. With Neuer's contract running out in the summer, the chance to truly make the Bayern goal his own appears likely in the not-too-distant future.

The match on Saturday was Neuer's 550th in the Bundesliga and he also became the oldest player in a league match in Bayern's history when he took the pitch aged 40 years and 225 days. In other words, he can't go on forever.

One of his most famous predecessors in the Bayern goal has already called on him to draw a line under his highly successful career.

"I would tell him: 'Call it a day, Manu!' You have given an incredible amount to football, you have won everything, and you don't have to prove anything to anyone anymore," Sepp Maier, a member of West Germany's 1974 World Cup winning team told Sport1.

In a recent development, at some point, the now 82-year-old Maier noted, there comes a moment "when your body no longer behaves the way you want it to. And even a Manuel Neuer cannot stave off that moment.".

Sources indicate that for now, with ter Stegen playing regularly and performing well for Ajax, Germany coach Klopp is under no pressure to make a change. However, the 34-year-old former Barcelona keeper has, like Neuer, become quite injury-prone in recent years. Whenever he's needed, Urbig will be more than happy to seize his opportunity.

One player who looked slightly bemused as to why this was happening is third-choice goalkeeper Tom Heaton.

The 40-year-old, who has been around the block a few times, gave a cheeky look towards the cameras as if to say “yes, we are doing performative weight training on the side of the pitch.”.

All of this is part of Project Pochettino which aims to turn the unbothered United squad into one of the hardest-working in the Premier League.

But he will want to start winning games as soon as possible and suggested they should have on Wednesday night.

“I think we dominated and we deserved to win the game, but we didn’t for different circumstances,” he noted.

“All the teams make mistakes, but for these mistakes the punishment is too major in every single mistake. Many other clubs make mistakes or tilt in a different circumstance, in a more positive way. But that is in the way we are. We need to take responsibility.”.

READ: The 11 Man Utd players out on loan in 2026-27 & how they’ve been faring.

Pochettino may also have a problem in goal after Senne Lammens, who at one point in his United career looked like a much-needed safe pair of hands, spilt an easy catch for Sporting’s second.

Pochettino, though, defended his player and remarked these things happen.

“This type of thing happens,” he remarked. “That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

“I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s not to blame the defensive line, but it’s two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage this type of situation better.”.

Recent findings suggest that who indicates international truce often means housekeeping… And on the Manchester United side, after a catastrophic start to the season, Michael Carrick left. After a particularly good second part of the 2025/2026 season, having taken over from Ruben Amorim and qualifying the Red Devils for the Champions League, the former midfielder obtained catastrophic results at the start of the year. The Mancuniens are thus in a sad eighteenth place in the Premier League standings and they quickly paid the price.

Sources indicate that very rapidly, the name of Mauricio Pochettino appeared as the main candidate to replace him, ahead of other names like Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann. The North American coach maintains a superb rating across the Channel, where he had obtained excellent results with Southampton, then at Tottenham between 2014 and 2019, including a Champions League final. If his return to London with Chelsea during the 2023/2024 season did not necessarily go very well, the former PSG coach remains considered a top coach by our English neighbors.

It was therefore quite natural that Manchester United turned to him, while the Argentinian had also had the ambition, for a long time, to coach the Red Devils one day. The Mancunians confirmed his arrival until 2029 via an official press release this Friday: “Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to take charge of the Manchester United men’s team from November 18. The club has reached an agreement with the United States Soccer Federation so that Mauricio and his staff can be released from their duties once their assignments with the United States men’s national team are completed. ».

Note that they had to pay around nine million euros to snatch him from the United States selection, where he was under contract until 2030. The same for a good part of his staff. Pochettino will have a few days to discover his players – even if many are with their selection – and try to familiarize them with his methods before a huge meeting after the break: a shock against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday November 22. Baptism of fire for Pochettino therefore….

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of notable saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

In a recent development, “I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager mentioned. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

It has been revealed that “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

Sources indicate that “We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

According to recent reports, villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

It was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

Industry observers note that mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

Industry observers note that “We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”.

#141471. The story of Eric Cantona and his incredible impact on Man Utd

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1836 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Planetfootball ↗ Open Full Page

The story of Eric Cantona and his incredible impact on Man Utd

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1836 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On May 17, 1997, Eric Cantona confirmed his retirement from football.
  • It has been revealed that “‘Ooh ahh, Cantona’?
  • That was one of the more extreme responses from a supporter outside Old Trafford (see video below) the day after Cantona stunned football – not for the first time and certainly not for the last – by signing for Manchester United.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On May 17, 1997, Eric Cantona confirmed his retirement from football. He was only 30 years old, but his impact on Manchester United and on English football had been immeasurable.

It has been revealed that “‘Ooh ahh, Cantona’? They won’t sing it here.”.

That was one of the more extreme responses from a supporter outside Old Trafford (see video below) the day after Cantona stunned football – not for the first time and certainly not for the last – by signing for Manchester United.

As a 12-year-old red growing up in a Leeds United heartland, I certainly wasn’t sure how to process the breaking story late in the Calendar News bulletin at 6.25pm on Thursday, November 26, 1992.

Cantona had played a significant part in my misery up to that point, and his chant had provided the backing music for some merciless stick at school six months earlier when he helped Leeds deny my team their first Championship in 25 years. Yet here he was, switching sides.

Alex Ferguson did little to reassure his club’s supporters that there was method to the madness when he admitted Cantona only came into his mind “more or less” when Leeds called to enquire about Denis Irwin.

Cantona had only joined Leeds in January, signed for £900,000 by Howard Wilkinson from Nimes, and though the then-24-year-old made only six starts and another nine appearances off the bench in the second half of that 1991-92 season, his cameos helped Leeds beat Ferguson’s men to the title.

Cantona’s three goals came at home against teams in the lower half of the table, but he got the ball rolling against Luton and Wimbledon and broke Chelsea’s resistance with one of the goals of the season.

With Cantona, Leeds took 13 points from their final five games of the run-in, while Man Utd drew one and lost three on the spin against Nottingham Forest, West Ham and Liverpool to almost gift-wrap the final pre-Premier League title for their Yorkshire rivals.

Though Ferguson acknowledged in both autobiographies that Leeds were worthy champions, his side unquestionably blew it as his fear over the goals drying up became a reality.

It has been revealed that coincidence though it may be, when Leeds signed Cantona, Man Utd were averaging 2.9 goals per game over 26 matches. In the final 16-game run-in, that plummeted to one goal per game, while they were shut out six times.

Sixteen games into the following campaign, United were eighth and again averaging only a goal per game when a call took place which changed the face of English football.

“I remember that phone call clearly, as though it was yesterday,” Leeds’ former Managing director Bill Fotherby stated in 2012.

“We agreed to pay Eric something like £500,000 if we kept him after the initial period of six months. It was an immense amount of money for Leeds, but we agreed to it because we had this recommendation from Michel Platini and we judged the most important thing was to get the player.

Recent findings suggest that “We wanted to do whatever it took and deal with the rest afterwards. But there were difficulties almost immediately.

According to recent reports, “Apart from Lee Chapman, no-one in the squad spoke fluent French, and for Howard, it was a bit of a nightmare. Although we had won the title, there was just no connection between the two and, in the end, he told me to try and find Eric another club.

“Howard Wilkinson was an absolute perfectionist. He wanted his players to be disciplined and adhere to a certain team pattern. Eric just didn’t fit it.

While Cantona might not have been suited to Leeds, he found his perfect match across the Pennines.

“If ever there was one player, anywhere in the word, that was made for Manchester United, it was Cantona,” mentioned Ferguson later.

“He swaggered in, stuck his chest out, raised his head and surveyed everything as though he were asking: ‘I’m Cantona. How big are you? Are you big enough for me?’”.

Ince, the self-styled Guvnor, mentioned Cantona “took the responsibility away from us lot”, which was evident from the manner in which United attacked the second half of the season.

They doubled their goals per game over the remaining 26 matches, netting 50 times in 18 wins, losing only twice on their way to breaking a 26-year title drought. Famine was about to become feast.

Ferguson had been searching for a goalscorer, but in Cantona he found something rarer. The Frenchman notched nine goals over the remainder of the season, perhaps not a Shearer-esque strike-rate, but he offered 11 assists.

More than anything tangible, Cantona brought a swagger and a confidence which often strutted over the border to an arrogance that so inspired his team-mates and wowed fans at the now Stretford End-less Old Trafford.

With Bryan Robson’s powers waning, Cantona arrived at the perfect time. Countless team-mates have referenced how the Frenchman became the example to follow at The Cliff. They had a newly introduced leader.

Even Ferguson admits Cantona “opened my eyes to the indispensability of practice”.

Sources indicate that with Cantona leading the line, United felt and often looked invincible. The burden of responsibility Ince referred to was gone, and they followed up the title in 1993 with their first-ever Double in 1994.

Industry observers note that cantona, with his collar up, was at the heart of all that the purists identified as good and bad about that 93-94 team. He scored 25 goals in all competitions and contributed 13 assists, earning himself the PFA Player of the Year award.

There was no sign of the temper United had been warned about until the Champions League trip to Galatasaray in November 1993 when Cantona received his first red card in a United shirt for insulting the referee, who he later accused of being “bought”.

As he and his team-mates descended down the steps towards the underground changing rooms, Cantona was slyly attacked by a baton and shield-wielding policeman, as was Robson when the skipper rushed to defend his team-mate.

In a recent development, “In the dressing room, Eric went crazy,” Roy Keane recalled in his autobiography. “While the rest of us just wanted to get out of there, Eric was determined to sort out the rogue cop who had been wielding his truncheon.

“Eric was a massive, strong lad. He was serious. He insisted he was going to kill that f***er. It took the combined efforts of the manager, Brian Kidd and a few of the players to restrain him.”.

Much like supporters, Cantona’s blood boiled at the thought of any perceived injustice, and that connection made it easy for United fans to not only forgive Eric’s misdemeanours but to revel in them.

In a recent development, cantona simmered over later that season when he was banned for five games after red cards in successive draws at Swindon and Arsenal. But those incidents were merely child’s play compared to what was to come at Crystal Palace the following season.

The kung-fu kick on Matthew Simmons was the release of 48 minutes of frustration after Cantona had felt he had been kicked around Selhurst Park without any protection from Alan Wilkie.

Cantona questioned the referee at half-time while, according to Wilkie, Ferguson was more direct: “Why don’t you do your f*cking job!”.

Three minutes after emerging from the tunnel for the second half, Cantona was being directed back towards it after dishing out his own form of justice to his shadow for the night, Richard Shaw.

We all know what happened next.

Ferguson claims he has “never been able to elicit an explanation from Eric” as to why he felt the need to react to Matthew Simmons that way. Unsurprisingly, it seems he did it because he felt like it.

“Millions of times people say these things, and then one day you don’t accept it,” Cantona remarked.

In a recent development, “Why? It’s not about words. It’s about how you feel at that moment. One day you react, but the words are exactly the same as those you have heard a million times, so it is impossible to say why you react.”.

Cantona was subsequently suspended for nine months by the FA, and United went on to miss out on the title by a single point to Blackburn before losing the FA Cup final to Everton a week later.

To make matters worse, the FA threatened to extend Cantona’s suspension because he had been photographed taking part in a friendly against Rochdale that was nothing more than a behind-closed-doors kickabout of three thirds.

Cantona reacted by submitting a transfer request in early August.

Inter Milan, who were at Selhurst Park on that night in January to scout Cantona, would have been delighted to offer him a haven in Italy, but Ferguson travelled to Paris to convince his star player to stay put.

He later described that journey as “one of the more worthwhile acts I have performed in this stupid job of mine”.

Given the success that followed, that must rate as one of Ferguson’s greatest understatements. Another Double, this time with kids, and an additional Premier League title after that certainly justified his decision to smooth the path back for Cantona.

Cantona’s critics question his record, especially in European competition – though a goal every other game over six seasons and an assist for every three of his 185 appearances certainly stands up to scrutiny.

But Cantona’s contribution cannot be assessed by numbers.

According to recent reports, united fans remember the moments. The good ones were incredible, and even the bad ones were great.

Key goals, like the volley at Newcastle to break Kevin Keegan’s heart or the retreating shot from the edge of the box to win the 1996 FA Cup final against Liverpool’s Spice Boys.

And great goals too, against Sunderland or an even better lob in a gale at Sheffield United.

Eric Cantona vs Sheffield United, 1995. pic.twitter.com/CukcNEykQm.

— 90s Football (@90sfootball) June 27, 2020.

In terms of technique, Cantona was the best Old Trafford had seen for some time, but with regard to charisma, he was perhaps the greatest ever.

According to recent reports, robson will always be revered – despite not being a United product, he was the Stretford End’s representative on the pitch. Work hard, play hard, tackle harder, Captain Marvel was easy to relate to, but Eric was an enigma as well as an icon.

Never misunderstood at Old Trafford but being barely understood by his public certainly added to the mercurial Frenchman’s charm.

Like many of us were told about Best, Law and Charlton, there is now a generation of supporters who were never lucky enough to experience Cantona first-hand, and no amount of YouTube highlights videos can make those poor souls feel what Eric made United fans feel in the 1990s.

#141470. Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1459 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1459 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious.
  • But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.
  • This is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious. In 1941, Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler himself compared Eastern Europe to "Germany's India" after the British colonial model, declaring that "like the English, we shall rule this empire with a handful of men.".

But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.

This is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust. Others have argued that the intense focus on the Nazi era has, at least in part, come at the expense of a meaningful reckoning with Germany's colonial history.

Industry observers note that "I do think this is nonsense," says Stephan Malinowski, a Professor of Modern European History at the University of Edinburgh. "If it were true, then all other colonial countries who are not discussing the Holocaust, like Great Britain for example, or France or Spain or Portugal, they would then supposedly be very, very attentive to colonial crimes and to colonial history, which it seems to me is not the case.".

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence," a new exhibition at the German Historical Museum in Berlin curated by Malinowski, does not aim to settle the debate but to tell its story.

Recent findings suggest that the exhibition begins with a hippopotamus-hide whip used in African colonies displayed alongside a canister of Zyklon B, the poison used in Nazi gas chambers. The juxtaposition highlights the contrast between colonial violence and the industrialized mass murder of the Holocaust.

Yet it also points to connections: Whips were used in Nazi concentration camps, while Fascist Italy deployed chemical weapons against civilians and soldiers during its invasion of Ethiopia (then Abyssinia) in 1935-36.

In the 1930s, anti-colonial thinkers from India to the Caribbean argued that colonialism and fascism were two sides of the same coin. "There is nothing new or original about the blustering exploits of Hitler and Mussolini," observed the Trinidadian journalist and Pan-Africanist George Padmore in 1938. "They have all been used before by the British in their efforts to obtain the subjection of less powerfully armed and more industrially backward people.".

European colonial rule was marked by the ruthless exploitation of people and resources, often enforced through extreme violence. In "The Origins of Totalitarianism" (1951), German-American philosopher Hannah Arendt argued that colonial territories served as laboratories for racial ideologies and practices of domination that could be applied beyond the legal constraints of Europe. Arendt described how these later "boomeranged" back into Europe and helped shape totalitarian politics in distinct and unprecedented form.

The Congo Free State, King Leopold II of Belgium's private colony from 1885 to 1908, became notorious for its extreme brutality, as colonial authorities used executions, amputations and sexual violence to ensure rubber production quotas were met.

Recent findings suggest that forced labor was also central to Nazi rule, with millions of Poles, Ukrainians, Russians and others from the Soviet Union, and Jews, subjected to exploitation and "Vernichtung durch Arbeit" ("extermination through work"). Within a few years, the regime mobilized around 13 to 14 million forced laborers, a scale comparable to the transatlantic slave trade over more than three centuries. The Nazis sought to extract value from their victims at every stage, confiscating their property, exploiting their labor, and even harvesting gold teeth and hair from the dead.

Sources indicate that while racism underpinned both colonial empires and Nazism, Malinowski indicates the goals were different. The colonial powers tended to present assimilation as a path to advancement, forcing colonized people to adopt European culture, serve imperial interests, and suggesting that a select, educated few could gain opportunities, for example at elite institutions such as Oxford or Cambridge. "This is definitely not something that the Nazi regime is offering to Poles or to Russians or let alone to Jews," added Malinowski.

In a recent development, "In terms of violence, colonial violence was just as extreme as Nazi violence. But Nazi violence was annihilatory and exterminatory compared to colonial violence in the colonies," says Edward Kissi, a historian at the School of Interdisciplinary Global Studies at the University of South Florida. He points to the example of how, unlike European colonial powers in Africa, the Nazis pursued the elimination of Black-Germans or peoples of African descent in Germany through forced sterilization. "Even in racism, colonial color-based racism and colonial anti-Jewish sentiments were fundamentally different from what the Nazis pursued.".

According to recent reports, on October 2, 1904, German General Lothar von Trotha issued the "Vernichtungsbefehl" ("extermination order") following the Herero uprising in German South West Africa (present-day Namibia). Historians generally attribute the order to a combination of racial ideology, a desire to terrorize the population into submission, and efforts to secure colonial control over land, labor and resources. Between 1904 and 1908, an estimated 60,000 to 80,000 Herero (around 80% of the population) and 10,000 (around half the population) Nama died.

One area where the exhibition draws no direct parallel is the industrialized killing carried out in Nazi death camps such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, and Auschwitz-Birkenau. "Where the two things really diverge is the Holocaust and is the systematic mass murder of the European Jews and it's murder for the very purpose of murder," explains Malinowski. The deportation of around 1,800 Jews from the Greek islands of Rhodes and Kos in July 1944 illustrates how Nazi persecution often defied military or economic logic. Even after the war was effectively lost, the community was transported to Auschwitz, where most were murdered immediately upon arrival.

It has been revealed that the problem of the "singularity" of the Holocaust came to the fore during the 1980s "Historikerstreit" ("historians' dispute"). Historian Ernst Nolte argued that Nazism should be understood in the wider context of 20th-century political violence, and as a response to Bolshevik terror in particular. Critics accused him of downplaying German responsibility for Nazi crimes.

Recent findings suggest that since 2020, a renewed debate dubbed the "Historikerstreit 2.0" has focused on whether the Holocaust should be viewed as a unique reference point in German memory culture or be understood alongside the histories of colonialism, racism and empire. The dispute now is less about the legitimacy of comparison than about its implications.

It has been revealed that the mass murder of tens of thousands of the Herero and Nama during four years of German colonial rule is now regarded as the first genocide of the 20th-century. But in 2016, Nama representatives walked out of talks after Germany's chief negotiator remarked what happened was "incomparable" to the Holocaust. The German government has since recognized the events as genocide "from today's perspective," but it has not yet accepted legal liability or agreed to pay formal reparations.

It has been revealed that martinican intellectual Aime Cesaire argued in "Discourse on Colonialism" (1950) that Europe condemned under Nazism forms of violence it had long accepted in its colonies. More than 70 years later, the exhibition opens amid renewed debates over the definition of settler colonialism and genocide, and the meaning of "never again," sharpened by Nicaragua's case against Germany at the International Court of Justice over Germany's support for Israel during the war in Gaza and its alleged failure to uphold its obligations under the Genocide Convention to prevent genocide.

These tensions are reflected in visitors' comments in the exhibition's epilogue, even though the exhibition itself does not address Israel or Palestine beyond a reference to Mohammed Amin al-Husseini, appointed Grand Mufti of Jerusalem in 1921.

It has been revealed that germany has unequivocally accepted responsibility for the Holocaust, which is front and center of the country's culture of remembrance. However, Kissi likens Germany's apparent reluctance to reckon with its colonial history to debates in the US over slavery, in Cambodia over the Khmer Rouge, and in Turkey over the Armenian genocide. According to him, Germany's contemporary identity cannot be fully understood without examining its colonial history and the ways the Nazis appropriated and transformed aspects of that legacy.

"I think Germans and all other human beings who have experienced violent pasts and difficult pasts should be very careful not to delink or dissociate those facts from their present," Kissi said. "These are historical patterns. It is better to deal with these historical patterns and discomforts than to just fight them and then say this has absolutely nothing to do with German national identity.".

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence" is on show at the German Historical Museum until April 11, 2027.

French team: the winners and losers of this November gathering

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the November gathering was rich in lessons for the French team.
  • In a recent development, this gathering allowed several players to stand out and score points in the minds of the staff.
  • Industry observers note that available, accurate in his transmissions and involved in defensive efforts, he displayed a particularly attractive face.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the November gathering was rich in lessons for the French team. With a victory against Turkey and a defeat against Italy, the Blues experienced two contrasting encounters, but ultimately achieved their objective by validating their qualification for the rest of the Nations League. This Sunday, the content left something to be desired, particularly on the defensive level and in the intensity of the pressing and which provoked the ire of Zinedine Zidane after the meeting. Obviously, several individuals scored points during this gathering, while others may have lost credit for the Blues’ upcoming games.

In a recent development, this gathering allowed several players to stand out and score points in the minds of the staff. This is particularly the case ofAndy Dioufwho took advantage of the playing time granted to show the extent of his qualities. Active on the left flank of the defense, the Inter Milan midfielder displayed great availability, with a real ability to project himself forward and support offensives. His activity in recovery, his investment in defensive work and his desire to play forward were also interesting. Everything was not perfect but in a position that was not very well provided, the Interist clearly highlighted that Zidane could count on him. Lucas Da Cunha is also one of the major winners of this gathering. After a good performance against Italy, the midfielder was particularly convincing against Turkey, delivering a successful match in midfield. Technically comfortable, he stood out for his quality of passing, his vision of the game and his ability to quickly find his partners in space.

Industry observers note that available, accurate in his transmissions and involved in defensive efforts, he displayed a particularly attractive face. For his second rally, Da Cunha has almost already established himself as an indisputable player in the midfield. Finally, Eli Junior Kroupiscorer against the Turks, is also one of the players who scored points during this international window. The young striker was able to take advantage of this experience with the Blues to get a little closer to the group and show his qualities. His offensive profile, his mobility and his willingness to provide solutions in the last meters constitute interesting arguments for the future. In a sector where competition is particularly high, each gathering represents an opportunity to stand out and gain credit with the staff. These three players took advantage of this period to send positive signals, with the hope of continuing this dynamic with a view to the Final 8 of the Nations League next March.

Among the successful firsts, we must necessarily mention Saël Kumbedi. A mystery guest on Zinédine Zidane’s list and summoned following Pierre Kalulu’s withdrawal, the former OL player was sharp for his first start this Sunday against Turkey. Not flamboyant, however, the Wolfsburg right-back showed that he was a credible candidate for the next gatherings even if the returns of Jules Koundé and Pierre Kalulu could obscure his international future in the long term. In any case, he scored points, unlike another player who we will talk about later, and showed that he can rejoin the group in the future in case of absences. In this line, Ibrahima Konate (re)applied to ZZ. Getting better and better with Real Madrid, the central defender was the author of a good rally and a reassuring tenure in central defense against Turkey. Despite increased competition from William Saliba, Dayot Upamecano, Maxence Lacroix and Jérémy Jacquet, the 27-year-old rock has shown that he is clearly fit to claim a place in the squad in the future.

It has been revealed that and the happiness of Ibrahima Konaté causes the misfortune of Leny Yoro. While the numerous absences in defense could allow him to accumulate playing time and score points, the Manchester United defender ultimately did not play a single minute. The only outfield player in the group not to have played during this break, he could be the first fuse to blow with the returns of Lacroix and Saliba. Especially since Konaté seems to have taken a head start in the hierarchy. Yoro was therefore unable to seize the opportunity offered to him and could promptly see his chances of winning dwindle. On the other hand, the massive loser of this gathering is undoubtedly Malo Gusto.

Industry observers note that wandered against Italy, the Chelsea full-back did not even have the opportunity to redeem himself against Turkey. Worse, Kumbedi’s encouraging tenure may suggest that the latter has now passed him in the hierarchy. A worrying situation for Gusto, who is already struggling to get playing time at club level with Chelsea. In front, Bradley Barcola didn’t score any points either. While he had a great opportunity to express himself with the absences of Désiré Doué and Ousmane Dembélé, the Parisian winger delivered two fairly average performances against Italy and Turkey. Interesting in sequences, he especially gave the impression of often being disconnected from his partners. Not to mention his finish and his last gesture are still frustrating. To hope to maintain an crucial place in the offensive hierarchy, he will have to show more regularity and influence, especially since Kroupi’s return from injury and promising debut could reshuffle the cards.

According to recent reports, in the Lyonnais gang, Rayan Cherki is called to the stand. Even if he remains an crucial player in Zidane’s plans, the virtuoso must also remain vigilant. The Lyonnais has the full confidence of the coach and has once again demonstrated his ability to turn a match around thanks to his technical quality, by being involved in both goals against Turkey. But some of his choices and his body language can sometimes be annoying. His midfield positioning could also be called into question with the returns of Akliouche, Koné and Tchouaméni, especially if Zidane decides to reorganize his system. He nevertheless remains a real step ahead thanks to his valuable talent and his importance in offensive animation. Finally, in the goals, Robin Risser now appears officially relegated to third goalkeeper after Restes replaced Maignan against Turkey. A hierarchy which places him at the forefront among the players likely to leave the group if another goalkeeper were to perform and convince. In difficulty with RC Lens since the start of the season, the young Lensois goalkeeper, targeted by Bayern, will therefore have to remain efficient so as not to permanently lose his place at Clairefontaine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 05:24 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 02:27 EST, 26 November 2026.

Jude Bellingham has earned praise after the Real Madrid star insisted a female reporter was able to finish asking her questions in the mixed zone after being interrupted.

Bellingham spoke to media post-match after scoring the 'best goal of my life' in Real Madrid's 5-1 victory over PSV in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The England star had collected a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, initially controlling it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal.

Bellingham's stunning strike meant he was unsurprisingly in-demand post-match, with reporters eager to get his assessment of his goal.

BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had asked Bellingham in the mixed zone what had gone through his mind when he scored with his sensational effort.

'Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,' Bellingham noted. 'I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through.

Jude Bellingham has earned praise after the Real Madrid star insisted a female reporter was able to finish asking her questions in the mixed zone.

BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had been interrupted by a male reporter when asking her second question, leading to Bellingham's intervention. Source: instagram/@elizabeth.conway_.

Bellingham (right) had been in-demand after scoring with a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven.

'It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it.

'It was a nice goal and important for the team being the second goal and gave us control.'.

Conway looked to follow-up with a second question but was interrupted by a male reporter, leading to Bellingham intervening.

'Sorry, she's got one more,' Bellingham stated, while pointing to Conway to encourage her to continue her question.

When asked by Conway whether he feels like he is in the form of his life for club and country, Bellingham added: 'My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn't really matter.

'Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.'.

Conway later shared the exchange on social media, writing: 'Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,' adding a handshake emoji while fans were quick to praise Bellingham for his 'classy' moment.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked his goal, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley.

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net.

Bellingham is in advanced contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031.

His brother Jobe, who played in Borussia Dortmund's 1-1 draw with Arsenal on the same night, later joked that Jude's shot had 'come off his shin' before acknowledging it was a 'great goal'.

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho and captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho said. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'.

According to recent reports, valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advanced talks over a latest Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Live & Exclusive on Stan Sport.#StanSportAU #UCL pic.twitter.com/DpIzIUoXRy.

Rafael Nadal was seen celebrating Bellingham's stunning goal with his young son from the Real Madrid director's box.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a fresh deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

Footage shared on social media also showed tennis legend Rafael Nadal and his young son exuberantly celebrating Bellingham's stunning goal against PSV.

Nadal last week was officially elected to Real Madrid's board of directors at the club's Extraordinary General Assembly.

#141466. An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 29m • 📚 Deep Dive (5819 w)

An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a latest flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining right now drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

Latest Update: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (836 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany has slipped down the climate action ranking for the third consecutive year, with the former green leader now being outperformed by Brazil, Colombia and Romania.
  • In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.
  • It has been revealed that still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," mentioned Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany has slipped down the climate action ranking for the third consecutive year, with the former green leader now being outperformed by Brazil, Colombia and Romania.

In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.

It has been revealed that still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," mentioned Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement. Denmark is leading the way across all four categories assessed — energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and national climate policy. A total of 15 states, including Lithuania, Chile, and Morocco, received an overall "high" rating, which is two more than last year.

The European Union also moved up a spot, while Hungary jumped 21 places after the ousting of former prime minister Viktor Orban's government, which had repeatedly vetoed EU climate aims, dismissing them as a "utopian fantasy.".

The top three positions on the CCPI remained vacant again this year, as no country has yet done enough to meet global climate goals aimed at preventing worsening weather extremes and climate damage.

According to recent reports, "We are seeing a striking contrast," stated Burck. "Progress on climate action is often slow and in some countries, such as the United States, things are even moving backwards. But technologically and economically there is enormous momentum.".

According to recent reports, that momentum is apparent in record solar energy growth. Last year 75% of global electricity demand growth was met by the green energy source, according to energy think tank Ember's latest global electricity review. Investment in clean energy has also outpaced that in fossil fuels for multiple years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The rapid expansion of renewable technology, as well as the Iran War and a reduction in deforestation are behind a projected slight fall in emissions for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the CCPI.

"Governments have to act now to turn the momentum into sustained emissions reductions," said CCPI co-author Niklas Höhne of the NewClimate Institute, which compiles the report with environmental NGO Germanwatch.

Burck attributed Germany's worst ever performance in the category of national climate policy to current policies being pursued by Germany's economy minister Katherina Reiche.

"Measures that primarily aim to increase the use of natural gas, threaten to undermine progress in the energy transition and risk significantly worsening the conditions for renewable energy and electrification for many years to come," said Burck.

A European Commission report published on November 9 on the sidelines of the UN COP31 climate summit in Turkey remarked Germany was one of nine EU countries set to miss 2030 emissions reductions targets.

Germany is not alone in its disappointing ranking. The other G20 countries — the world's leading industrialized and emerging economies, responsible for around 80% of global CO2 emissions — also perform poorly.

The only exception among them is the United Kingdom, which ranks seventh and received a high rating, performing well in greenhouse gas emissions, energy use and climate policy. However, study authors rated it low for renewable energy expansion.

The G20's oil- and gas-producing countries occupy some of the lowest positions on the climate action table. The United States, which is the world's second largest emitter, languishes alongside Russia, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Canada around the bottom of the league, with an overall rating of "very low.".

It has been revealed that the hosts of this year's COP31, also received a "low" overall score. Australia, a major coal exporter with some of the world's highest per-capita emissions, ranks 54th, while Turkey, which is also heavily dependent on fossil fuels, comes in 53rd.

China is the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases and ranks 56th in the CCPI, receiving an overall rating of "very low." Its main weaknesses include its now high per-capita emissions and substantial energy consumption.

In a recent development, however, among the G20, China leads the way in renewable energy expansion. The country, which is five years ahead of schedule in reaching its goal of adding 1,200 GW of wind and solar capacity to the grid by 2030, also produces over 80% of the world's solar panels.

Several oil-producing countries, including Kazakhstan, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates, are also performing better than expected in the renewables category and "are significantly expanding their previously limited" capacity, noted the report.

The authors said these countries have significant potential to further expand renewables.

"In the Arab states in particular, very high per-capita emissions and an above-average level of electrification coincide with a relatively low existing share of renewable energy and enormous solar potential," said co-author Natalie Pelekh in a statement. "These are, in fact, ideal conditions for more ambitious climate action.".

This article was originally published in German.
